ASSESSMENT OF THE FRACTIONAL AND CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF CHARTAK RESERVOIR SLUDGE SEDIMENTS FOR SUSTAINABLE WATER MANAGEMENT

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)

ABSTRACT

Experts suggest that climate change is affecting Central Asian countries, leading to water scarcity, energy scarcity, food insecurity, and environmental damage. Therefore, urgent attention is required to improve the operational efficiency of water reservoirs, enhance their reliability, and prevent the reduction of their useful capacity due to siltation. This study examines the main factors contributing to the siltation of reservoirs and determines their characteristic features along their length. To assess the turbidity of the stream, samples of the stream and sediments were collected in specialized containers using a bar bathometer. Laboratory analysis of these samples revealed that the turbidity of the flow ranged from 1.92 g/L to 0.01 g/L. The sediment fraction in the reservoir consisted of 35-40% large particles (d=1.0-0.1 mm) and 50-60% small particles (d=0.05-0.001 mm). Additionally, the sediments were found to contain chemical trace elements such as nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and humus, which can increase agricultural productivity by contributing to the creation of fertile soil layers when delivered to cultivated fields through irrigation networks.
